data.claim: The post-command wave auto-stamp (ddflow/api/waves_auto.py keep_stamped) writes wave:N tag events into the primary checkout's .ddflow/events/ when the ddflow package that is RUNNING lives in a linked worktree whose primary is the managed repo.
data.falsifier: Guarding keep_stamped so it refuses when primary_checkout(package_parent()) equals the managed repo makes the same command append nothing; the regression test asserts no new wave:* tag lands.
data.mechanism: keep_stamped restamps whenever log.mark() changed during the command, only checking the [waves].auto_stamp knob — never that the running package is the installed code, so a worktree checkout's feature-under-test writes the shared live log.
data.probe: tests/test_waves_worktree_isolation.py: unfixed FAILED (assert _waves == {} got {'A': 'wave:0'}), fixed 2 passed.
data.question: Does running ddflow from a linked worktree of ddflow against that worktree's PRIMARY checkout append wave:N tag events to the live shared event log?
